elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "(i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb expressly states "USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "(ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: "(iii) where Kubient processes, stores or otherwise handles any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types, as required.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "(iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law."

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: The document contains no insurance obligation anywhere (no coverage, certificate, workers' compensation, E&O or cyber language), so a concise insertion under Section 14 (General Provisions) is the correct remedy for a 'missing' finding, and all-new wording is permitted for a missing clause.
All six preferred elements appear in operative language with the exact bases and amounts required; the fallback floors are also cleared, so the redline is position-complete at both levels.

Minimality holds: the drafter trimmed the model language's non-required extras ('at its own expense' and the one-year survival tail) and added no procedures, notice mechanics, additional-insured, waiver-of-subrogation or notice-of-cancellation requirements outside the checklist. No existing text was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent is preserved: nothing in Section 14 or clause 9(b)(iii) is contradicted, no cross-reference is disturbed, and the new paragraph creates no conflict with the security obligations already owed for visitor data.

Drafting nits to tidy (not defects in the checklist): (a) 'applicable Law' is capitalised — if 'Law' is not a defined term in this Agreement, lowercase it to 'applicable law' to avoid a dangling defined term; (b) the inserted paragraph carries no subsection letter although Section 14 uses lettered subsections — label it '(j)' for consistency; (c) confirm 'Term' is the defined term used by the term/renewal clause so the coverage period has a fixed anchor.
